edges.description: Cortical parenchymal infiltration and D-2-hydroxyglutarate release induce peritumoral neuronal hyperexcitability and tumor-associated epilepsy.

nodes.description: The 1p/19q codeletion results from an unbalanced translocation t(1;19)(q10;p10) occurring early in tumorigenesis. This leads to loss of tumor suppressor genes including CIC on 19q and FUBP1 on 1p. The codeletion is associated with oligodendroglial differentiation and exceptional chemosensitivity.

evidence.reference_title: [Oligodendroglioma, IDH Mutation and 1p/19q Codeletion].

evidence.reference_title: Identification of der(1;19)(q10;p10) in five oligodendrogliomas suggests mechanism of concurrent 1p and 19q loss.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent loss of the der(1;19)(p10;q10) then results in the simultaneous 1p and 19q loss observed in oligodendroglioma with retention of the der(1;19)(q10;p10) seen in these cases.

nodes.description: CIC (Capicua) on 19q13 is mutated in approximately 70% of oligodendrogliomas, FUBP1 on 1p31 is mutated in approximately 15-30%, and inactivating NOTCH1 mutations recur in a subset. Unmasked by 1p/19q loss of heterozygosity, these tumor suppressor mutations cooperate with IDH mutation to drive oligodendroglioma formation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CIC and FUBP1 contribute to human oligodendroglioma.
evidence.snippet: Among other changes, we found that the CIC gene (homolog of the Drosophila gene capicua) on chromosome 19q was somatically mutated in six cases and that the FUBP1 gene ... on chromosome 1p was somatically mutated in two tumors. Examination of 27 additional oligodendrogliomas revealed 12 and 3 more tumors with mutations of CIC and FUBP1, respectively, 58% of which were predicted to result in truncations of the encoded proteins.

Hence, tumor-derived IDH1 and IDH2 mutations reduce α-KG and accumulate an α-KG antagonist, 2-HG, leading to genome-wide histone and DNA methylation alterations.

nodes.description: The combination of IDH mutation, 1p/19q codeletion, TERT promoter mutation, and CIC/FUBP1 mutations drives infiltrative oligodendroglioma formation. These tumors retain oligodendroglial lineage markers and maintain high sensitivity to alkylating DNA-damaging agents.

evidence.reference_title: Vorasidenib in IDH1- or IDH2-Mutant Low-Grade Glioma.
evidence.snippet: IDH-mutant grade 2 oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas grow continuously, albeit slowly, infiltrate the normal brain, and eventually become aggressive tumors with accelerated tumor growth and neovascularization, reflected by appearance of contrast enhancement on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

nodes.description: Procarbazine, CCNU (lomustine), and vincristine (PCV) combination chemotherapy shows exceptional efficacy in 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas. RTOG 9402 and EORTC 26951 trials demonstrated major survival benefit for PCV added to radiation in anaplastic oligodendroglioma.

evidence.reference_title: Phase III trial of chemoradiotherapy for anaplastic oligodendroglioma: long-term results of RTOG 9402.
evidence.snippet: the median survival of those with codeleted tumors treated with PCV plus RT was twice that of patients receiving RT (14.7 v 7.3 years; HR = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.95; P = .03)

evidence.reference_title: Adjuvant procarbazine, lomustine, and vincristine chemotherapy in newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglioma: long-term follow-up of EORTC brain tumor group study 26951.
evidence.snippet: The addition of six cycles of PCV after 59.4 Gy of RT increases both OS and PFS in anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors. 1p/19q-codeleted tumors derive more benefit from adjuvant PCV compared with non-1p/19q-deleted tumors.

nodes.description: External beam radiation is standard for anaplastic oligodendroglioma. For grade 2 tumors, timing of radiation may be deferred in favorable cases.

evidence.snippet: If further treatment beyond surgery is deemed necessary, the standard of care is radiotherapy followed by PCV 75 .

nodes.description: Seizures are the most common presenting symptom, occurring in 70-90% of patients. The high seizure frequency is attributed to cortical involvement and slow growth pattern. Seizure control often improves with tumor treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Upregulating mutations in the TERT promoter commonly occur in adult malignant gliomas and are strongly associated with total 1p19q loss.
evidence.snippet: The frequency of mutation was particularly high among primary glioblastomas (70 %) and pure oligodendroglial tumors (74 %), while relatively low in diffuse astrocytomas and anaplastic astrocytomas (19 and 25 %, respectively).

nodes.description: Mutually exclusive hotspot mutations at C228T or C250T in the TERT promoter create de novo ETS transcription factor binding sites, upregulating TERT expression and reactivating telomerase. This is the disorder-specific telomere-maintenance lesion that lets the tumor clone escape replicative senescence. TERT promoter mutation is near-universal in tumors carrying both 1p/19q codeletion and IDH1/2 mutation, and is therefore effectively part of the molecular signature of this entity rather than a late progression event.

evidence.reference_title: Upregulating mutations in the TERT promoter commonly occur in adult malignant gliomas and are strongly associated with total 1p19q loss.
evidence.snippet: TERT promoter mutations were observed in almost all tumors harboring concurrent total 1p19q loss and IDH1/2 mutations (98 %).

evidence.reference_title: Upregulating mutations in the TERT promoter commonly occur in adult malignant gliomas and are strongly associated with total 1p19q loss.
evidence.snippet: The expression level of TERT in tumors carrying those mutations was on average 6.1 times higher than that of wild-type tumors, indicating that the mutated promoter leads to upregulation of TERT.

evidence.reference_title: Upregulating mutations in the TERT promoter commonly occur in adult malignant gliomas and are strongly associated with total 1p19q loss.
evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that mutation of the TERT promoter is one of the major mechanisms of telomerase activation in gliomas.

nodes.description: Temozolomide is used as a more tolerable alkylating alternative to PCV, often concurrently with radiation followed by adjuvant cycles. Its role as a substitute for radiotherapy is not supported: in the initial CODEL design, grade 3 codeleted patients randomized to temozolomide alone had significantly shorter progression-free survival than those on the radiotherapy arms, and the trial was redesigned to compare radiotherapy plus PCV against radiotherapy plus temozolomide rather than temozolomide alone. Temozolomide monotherapy in place of radiotherapy should therefore not be inferred from this entry.

evidence.reference_title: CODEL: phase III study of RT, RT + TMZ, or TMZ for newly diagnosed 1p/19q codeleted oligodendroglioma. Analysis from the initial study design.
evidence.snippet: TMZ-alone patients experienced significantly shorter PFS than patients treated on the RT arms.

evidence.reference_title: CODEL: phase III study of RT, RT + TMZ, or TMZ for newly diagnosed 1p/19q codeleted oligodendroglioma. Analysis from the initial study design.
evidence.snippet: The ongoing CODEL trial has been redesigned to compare RT + PCV versus RT + TMZ.

nodes.description: Oral, brain-penetrant dual inhibitor of the mutant IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes, FDA-approved in August 2024 for grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma with a susceptible IDH1/IDH2 mutation following surgery. It is the first therapy directed at the founding molecular lesion of this disease rather than at tumor bulk, and it is positioned in the post-surgical setting where radiotherapy and chemotherapy are being deferred. Transaminase elevation is the characteristic dose-limiting toxicity and requires liver function monitoring.

evidence.reference_title: Vorasidenib in IDH1- or IDH2-Mutant Low-Grade Glioma.
evidence.snippet: In patients with grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma, vorasidenib significantly improved progression-free survival and delayed the time to the next intervention.

evidence.reference_title: Vorasidenib in IDH1-mutant or IDH2-mutant low-grade glioma (INDIGO): secondary and exploratory endpoints from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Vorasidenib reduced tumour growth rate and improved seizure control compared with placebo, with no observed negative effects on HRQOL or neurocognition.
